source_read: Publisher HTML (Springer Nature Link, Harm Reduct J 21:159, open access), read in full in the built-in browser: all text sections (the page text stops at 50,000 characters inside the reference list; references, Acknowledgements, Funding, Conflict of interest and Supplementary list read with javascript_tool on the same tab); Fig. 2 (limit-of-detection grid) and Fig. 3 (cross-reactivity grid) read cell by cell on the full-size images. Figs. 1 and 4 seen only through their captions and text. Supplementary Material 1 (DOCX download, incl. 5-min readouts S3) not opened.

claims.note: De Vrieze part checked: the authors' closing paragraph says a negative result does not mean a sample is safe and a positive result gives no identity, quantity or purity; these are conclusions, not tested. The paper also supports 'nitazene ... strips missed some nitazenes' (9 of 33 not detected at 9000 ng/mL) and adds two reasons a negative may mislead that the claim could cite: amounts below the cut-off may still be dangerous, and incomplete dissolution was seen in every powder tested. It did not test whether line intensity shows amount.

anchors.extracted: Authors: a negative result does not imply a sample is safe, since it may still hold non-cross-reacting nitazenes, other synthetic opioids, other drugs or adulterants; a positive result gives no information on identity, quantity or purity of the nitazene(s); they advise reading a faint test line as positive in harm-reduction use. Stated as conclusions; not tested.

Nitazenes present below the strip cut-off may still cause dangerous opioid effects; desnitazenes such as metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene are unlikely to be picked up even in highly pure samples and may give a false sense of safety; detection may also be limited by solubility (all tested powders dissolved incompletely).
9 of 33 nitazene analogues (compounds 19-24, 26, 31-32) gave no positive reading at 9000 ng/mL.

claims.overstatement: Two wording points. (1) 'missed one group entirely' and 'the six desnitazenes' are not accurate: seven desnitazenes were tested and one, 5-methyl etodesnitazene (25), was detected (at 3000 ng/mL), which the authors call the only desnitazene found to cross-react; the misses were six of seven desnitazenes, 5-aminoisotonitazene and the two ethylene-linker analogues. Suggested: 'missed six of the seven desnitazenes and three other analogues'. (2) 'seized powders' is not what the paper says: the six were 'sourced' samples from Belgian Early Warning System routine market monitoring, two of them probably sold undiluted (one, N-pyrrolidino etonitazene, characterized earlier as sold online; refs 10 and 43); 'market-monitoring powders' would be accurate.
claims.note: All numbers from this source match: maker's cut-off 2000 ng/mL isotonitazene; limit (all six replicates positive, three days in duplicate) 3000 ng/mL lot A and 2000 ng/mL lot B, the same by visual and ImageJ scoring (Fig. 2); lots obtained about four months apart; cross-reactivity on lot B, one strip per compound and concentration; 24 of 33 positive at 9000 ng/mL or less (16 + 7 + 1 visually: counts confirmed from the compound lists and Fig. 3); 9 not at 9000 ng/mL; six powders all positive at about 1 and 0.1 mg/mL. Editors' Wilson 95% CI for 6/6 recomputed: 61.0-100%, same. Details: Fig. 2 shows positives below the limit on lot B (visual 2/6 at 750 and 1000 ng/mL; ImageJ 3/6 at 500), so readings near the cut-off scatter; lot A had no positive below 1500 (visual) or 3000 (ImageJ). Results are 10-min readings (5-min readings, with more indeterminates, are in the supplement). In Fig. 3 the visual retest of compound 16 is positive at 3000 ng/mL, while the text (and the claim's magnitude) puts it in 'positive only at 9000 ng/mL'. The raters were two of the authors, blinded to sample identity. The 12-sample street data (sensitivity 100% and 89%, specificity 100%) and the CFSRE screen are cited from the maker's white paper (ref. 41); the Sisco et al. limits the claim gives (metonitazene 1000, N-piperidinyl etonitazene and protonitazene 5000 ng/mL) are relayed identically in the Introduction. Only brorphine (1 mg/mL, negative) was tested for specificity.

anchors.extracted: Maker: strips calibrated with isotonitazene, cut-off 2000 ng/mL; three other analogues listed (1300-4500 ng/mL); metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene not detected at 100 µg/mL; no cross-reactivity with listed cutting agents and drugs at 100 µg/mL or more. From the maker's white paper (ref. 41): CFSRE detected 24 of 29 analogues at 3000 ng/mL, including metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene; Chicago Recovery Alliance preliminary data on 12 street samples, sensitivity 100% and 89% at 10 mg per 1 mL and per 5 mL, specificity 100%. Sisco et al. (ref. 42): limits 1000 (metonitazene), 5000 (N-piperidinyl etonitazene) and 5000 ng/mL (protonitazene).

anchors.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Nitazene test strip analysis, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Two lots (A DOAB23120001, B DOAB24010002), bought from a UK supplier; strips dipped 15 s, photographed at 5 and 10 min in a fixed set-up; maker's rule: any shade in the test area is negative. Two independent raters (authors) blinded to sample identity scored +, - or ?; no +/- disagreements. ImageJ scoring as a second method.

anchors.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Limit of detection, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Isotonitazene 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 3000 ng/mL in water (1.8% methanol) plus blank; each tested on three days with both lots in duplicate (six replicates); limit = lowest concentration with all replicates positive.

anchors.locator: Results › Limit of detection, 1st paragraph; Fig. 2
anchors.extracted: Limit 3000 ng/mL (lot A) and 2000 ng/mL (lot B) by both visual and ImageJ scoring. Fig. 2, positives out of 6: lot A visual 0 up to 1000, 1 at 1500, 2 at 2000 (rest indeterminate), 6 at 3000; lot A ImageJ 0 up to 2000, 6 at 3000; lot B visual 2 at 750, 2 at 1000, 3 at 1500, 6 at 2000 and 3000; lot B ImageJ 3 at 500, 2 at 750, 3 at 1000, 5 at 1500, 6 at 2000 and 3000; blanks all negative.
Lot B matched the 2000 ng/mL cut-off, lot A slightly higher; both lots obtained about four months apart, so major manufacturing changes were less likely.

anchors.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Fig. 3
anchors.extracted: 32 analogues plus isotonitazene on lot B: first at 3000 ng/mL (n = 1), then 1000 if positive, 9000 if negative, both if indeterminate; each compound tested once per concentration. 24 of 33 positive at 9000 ng/mL or less (compounds 1-18, 25, 27-30, 33); 9 not at 9000 (19-24, 26, 31-32). Visually 16 positive at 1000 and 3000, 7 at 3000 only, compound 16 at 9000 only; ImageJ 19 and 5. Sample volume within the strip markings did not change results; brorphine negative at 1 mg/mL.

Not detected: desnitazenes lacking the 5-nitro group (19-24), 5-aminoisotonitazene (26) and the two ethylene-linker analogues (31-32). 5-Methyl etodesnitazene (25), a desnitazene with a methyl at the 5-position, was detected at 3000 ng/mL; authors call it the only desnitazene found to cross-react. Metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene negative at 9000 ng/mL, unlike the CFSRE screen.

anchors.locator: Materials and methods › Materials, 1st paragraph; Materials and methods › Methods › Testing of authentic powder samples, 1st paragraph; Results › Testing of authentic powder samples, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Six 'sourced' powders from Belgian Early Warning System routine market monitoring (metonitazene, protonitazene, isotonitazene, butonitazene, two N-pyrrolidino etonitazene); LC-QTOF-MS estimated purity above 90% (peak-intensity ratio, with an ionization caveat). 1 mg in 1 mL tap water (about 1 mg/mL), then a 1:10 dilution (about 0.1 mg/mL), one strip each; undissolved powder in all; all positive at 5 and 10 min, visually and by ImageJ; tap-water blank included. 6/6, Wilson 95% CI 61.0-100% (recomputed).

Specificity not re-tested apart from brorphine; authors call for studies of authentic street samples for false positives and false negatives. The powders were probably pure and may not represent real-world samples; testing of mixtures is needed; two powders probably sold undiluted.

A negative result does not mean a sample is safe (may contain non-reacting nitazenes, other opioids, other drugs); a positive gives no identity, quantity or purity; authors advise treating a faint test line as positive in harm reduction.

No invalid strips; all negative controls negative; test lines always fainter than control lines; fewer indeterminate scores at 10 than at 5 min, so 10-min readings are reported (5-min in Supplementary S3).

key_findings.note: The two raters were two of the authors (L.D.V. and M.V.), blinded to sample identity.

Replicate-level values from Fig. 2 (positives out of 6): lot A visual 0 at 500-1000, 1 at 1500, 2 at 2000 (others indeterminate), 6 at 3000; lot A ImageJ 0 at every concentration up to 2000, 6 at 3000; lot B visual 0 at 500, 2 at 750, 2 at 1000, 3 at 1500, 6 at 2000 and 3000; lot B ImageJ 3 at 500, 2 at 750, 3 at 1000, 5 at 1500, 6 at 2000 and 3000; blanks 0. Lot B thus gave positive readings at 25-50% of the cut-off, contrary to the maker's statement that samples at 50% of the cut-off read all negative.

key_findings.correction: Text and Fig. 3 differ for compound 16: in Fig. 3 the visual retest of N-piperidinyl etonitazene is positive at 3000 ng/mL (first test indeterminate), and positive at 9000 in both tests, so if the retest replaces the first result, as the text says it does for the categorization, compound 16 belongs visually with the compounds positive at 3000 ng/mL (8 instead of 7) and none is positive only at 9000 ng/mL. The text's 16/7/1 split, which the card and the claim's magnitude follow, uses the first visual test for compound 16.

'Six seized powders': the paper calls them 'sourced' powders obtained in the Belgian Early Warning System's routine drug-market monitoring (Materials and methods › Materials, 1st paragraph) and never says they were seized; two (isotonitazene and one N-pyrrolidino etonitazene) were characterized earlier as pure and probably sold undiluted (Discussion, 7th paragraph), one in a paper on a product sold online (ref. 43). Use 'six market-monitoring powders'. The same word appears in design_detail, sample.n_by_group and the sample-selection domain note. The rest of the finding is confirmed, including the editors' Wilson interval (recomputed 61.0-100%).

key_findings.note: Reference 41, the source of the CFSRE and Chicago Recovery Alliance figures, is the maker's 2024 white paper; the Sisco et al. limits are from reference 42 (Forensic Chem 2024;40:100594).
Editors' 0.1-0.3% recomputed (2000 ng/mL in 2 mg/mL; 3000 ng/mL in 1 mg/mL). The authors' 0.9% end corresponds to 9000 ng/mL at 1 mg/mL.

reporting_issues.note: Halifax et al. 2024: levamisole no cross-reactivity up to 100 mg/mL (2021 lots); Lockwood et al. 2021 did not test levamisole; both checked in this round.
Fig. 3 row 7: isotonitazene positive at 1000 and 3000 ng/mL, visual and ImageJ.
Add the text-figure mismatch for compound 16's visual retest at 3000 ng/mL (key finding 5), which makes its visual category uncertain as well.
The paper does not state the maker's reading time, so whether 10 min departs from the insert cannot be told from the text.
Reference 40 is the BTNX nitazene product insert (2023); reference 50 is a New Zealand Drug Foundation web page.

risk_of_bias.note: Sample selection high, reference standard low, flow and timing unclear, overall high: agree. Index test low is defensible (raters blinded to identity, indeterminate category, a second automated scoring), though the reading time (10 min) was chosen after seeing that it gave fewer indeterminate scores and the raters were authors; some appraisers would rate it unclear. This does not change the overall judgment.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor agreed. The abstract's 'no observed false negatives' rests on six nearly pure powders tested well above the limit, as the card says; the authors otherwise state their limits clearly (Discussion, 7th and 8th paragraphs).

missed: Powders are 'sourced' market-monitoring samples, not seized (see key finding 8); the card uses 'seized' in four places.

Fig. 2 replicate data: lot B read positive in some replicates from 500-750 ng/mL (25-38% of the cut-off), against the maker's statement that 50% of the cut-off reads all negative; lot A had no ImageJ positive below 3000 ng/mL. Readings near the cut-off scatter widely, which matters for any claim that treats 2000-3000 ng/mL as a sharp limit.
Fig. 3: visual retest of compound 16 positive at 3000 ng/mL, contrary to the text's 'positive only at 9000 ng/mL' (key finding 5).
